EmailTemplate.subject: PhD degree in biomedical engineering at ASU
EmailTemplate.textOnly:
Thank you for your interest in the nationally ranked MS program in biomedical engineering at Arizona State University. ASU’s School of Biological and Health Systems Engineering is actively engaged in pushing the boundaries of science, medicine and engineering in areas ranging from cardiovascular engineering, biovirtual reality and neuroengineering to synthetic biology, tissue engineering and regenerative medicine. The Master of Science degree in biomedical engineering is a rigorous 30-credit hour program in which you will be guided by our world-class faculty to complete courses within your focus area and complete either a thesis or an applied project.
Areas of study include:
biomaterials, biosensors, biomarkers and biomimetic materials
molecular, cellular and tissue engineering
neural and rehabilitation engineering
synthetic and systems biology
biomedical imaging
Application process and requirements must be completed to be considered, including priority deadlines, letters of recommendation, financial assistance, and prerequisites.
(There are no minimum GRE test scores required to gain entrance into the program. However, competitive scores increase an applicant’s likelihood of acceptance. The most recent average GPA of admitted applicants was 3.45, while the average GRE sub scores were 154, 156 and 3.8 for verbal, quantitative, and analytical, respectively.)
English proficiency requirements have been established by the Office of Graduate Education.
Research opportunities are available for graduate students of all levels to increase knowledge in their discipline while improving an understanding of industry-used practices and procedures.
Please contact our office should you have any additional questions during your application process.
Kind regards,
